title: Unit and coefficient associativity of compact-support projection maps
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ of its valuation ring, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to Y$ be separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix a compactification $c=(j,r)$ with $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Work in the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Put $P=Rf_!^c=Rr_*j_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] and $S=Lf^*$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with its canonical strong monoidal structure [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso, def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $\delta_{B,B'}:S(B\otimes B')\xrightarrow{\sim}SB\otimes SB'$ and $e:S\mathbf1_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_X$ be its inverse structure maps. Here $\mathbf1_T=A_T$ in degree zero, and $\otimes$ denotes the derived tensor.
For $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], use exactly the compactification projection transformation $\operatorname{PF}^c_{M,B}:PM\otimes B\to P(M\otimes SB)$ of [def-exchange-projection]. Where these maps are invertible, define
$$\pi_{B,M}:P(SB\otimes M)\xrightarrow{P(\beta_{SB,M})}P(M\otimes SB)\xrightarrow{(\operatorname{PF}^c_{M,B})^{-1}}PM\otimes B\xrightarrow{\beta_{PM,B}}B\otimes PM,$$
where $\beta$ is tensor symmetry. Invertibility is a separate hypothesis here, not part of the conclusion.
These inverse projection maps satisfy the unit and coefficient-variable associativity equations of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. Explicitly, for $B,B'\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$, whenever all projection components in the following expressions are invertible,
$$\lambda_{PM}\circ\pi_{\mathbf1_Y,M}=P\bigl(\lambda_M\circ(e\otimes1_M)\bigr),$$
$$\alpha_{B,B',PM}\circ\pi_{B\otimes B',M}
=(1_B\otimes\pi_{B',M})\circ\pi_{B,SB'\otimes M}\circ P\bigl(\alpha_{SB,SB',M}\circ(\delta_{B,B'}\otimes1_M)\bigr).$$
Here $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ are the canonical derived tensor associator and left unitor, and all equations are equalities of derived morphisms at the fixed compactification. All displayed tensor inputs belong to the stated constructible domains; one coefficient factor of finite Tor amplitude suffices for each product with $M$. No right adjoint to $P$, smoothness, purity, or compatibility with composition of two geometric morphisms is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: Conjugate the right projection action by canonical tensor symmetries. Naturality, the two hexagons, symmetry squared equal to identity, and compatibility of derived pullback with symmetry give the forward left coefficient-associativity law. The right unit law gives the left unit law. For precisely the four assumed invertible components, the displayed inverseCompactificationProjection is inverse to the conjugated action. Cancel these components to obtain exactly the two asserted equations.

proof.text: Transport intrinsic bounded constructibility and Tor amplitude to the canonical fixed-ring categories by intrinsic realization and lem-exc-intrinsic-tor-amplitude-transport. Standard coefficient theorems give the constructible finite-Tor tensor unit, stability under pullback and tensor, and bounded constructibility of a tensor whenever one factor is constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Symmetry treats either order. Finally transport the existing compact-support constructibility theorem to the chosen compactification using its canonical comparison; assemble the complete displayed list of domains. No Tor hypothesis on M and no absolute separatedness hypothesis are used.

A script confirmed that all nine base step texts appear verbatim in the report, and I traced where each one went. The three new statement-only nodes are 1842, 2061 and 1817 chars and the four-step assembly is 2347 chars. No argument was shortened. (1) lem-pur-adjoint-left-projection-action (base Steps 2-proper, 3, 4) is true. Here ρ is the adjunct of (ε⊗1)δ, which is exactly π_p in def-exchange-projection and Stacks 0B56. The transpose (1⊗ε)δ follows from counit naturality, F symmetric and β²=1. The unit law follows from the unit axiom of def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor. Associativity follows from (1) used twice plus the associativity axiom. No invertibility is used. (2) lem-pur-open-left-projection-action (base Steps 2-open, 5) is true. On Hom(JX,Y), f↦Q(f)u is the adjunction bijection, so Q is injective on maps out of objects isomorphic to ones in im J. Both sources qualify, through λ and through v (an isomorphism). I wrote out both reductions, via the normalization and Q's monoidal axioms. Its hypotheses match the statement of lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization: invertible unit, fully faithful j_!, and j^*γ equal to the identity after the unit and μ_j; for constant A its γ is the map that def-exchange-projection uses. (3) lem-pur-composite-left-projection-action (base Steps 6, 7) is true. It uses naturality of t at v, the t-law, the v-law at (FB,FB'), naturality of v at δ^F, and a^Q(Qδ^F⊗1)=a^S; the unit case is the same with e_F. Assembly Step 2: T = R(v)t after one cancellation of a β-pair, written out against the PF^c composite. Step 3's inversion order matches def-sfb-projection-formula. Step 4's hypotheses were checked against lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude, lem-sf-tensor-ctf (i)/(ii) and prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility, and M never needs finite Tor. Possible duplicates checked: lem-pur-finite-projection-action-laws is the geometric right-coefficient identity in another unit and has no unit law or detection argument. lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-associativity, lem-sfb-ringed-projection-canonical-normalization, lem-sfb-monoidal-adjunction-unit-counit, lem-amb-compactification-projection-composition and lem-asd-adjunction-projection-map-mate state other things.
